note: Questionnaire and condition-based screening rules for vehicle assessments. Keep this file byte-identical to Back-End/app/libraries/assessment_catalog.json; tests compare both copies. Thresholds are general workshop guidance, not manufacturer limits.

training_policy.note: Set before any model was trained. Change it only with a reason, never to make a specific model pass.

fair.reason: A Fair rating means wear or a defect was seen that does not yet need immediate work.
fair.action: Monitor at the next reassessment and plan service if it worsens.

poor.reason: A Poor rating means the assessor found a defect that needs repair.
poor.action: Schedule repair and confirm the condition with a mechanic.

critical.reason: A Critical rating means the assessor found the component unsafe or unfit for use.
critical.action: Stop using the vehicle for rentals until a mechanic has inspected and cleared this component.

questions.text: Does the engine start normally?
Does the engine idle smoothly?
Is the engine oil level within the dipstick range?
Is there a visible oil or fuel leak?
Is the check engine light on?

symptoms.label: Fuel leak or strong fuel smell

questions.text: Are the battery terminals clean and tight?
Does the starter crank strongly?
Do all exterior lights work?
Is the battery or charging warning light on?
Is the brake pedal firm?
Is the brake fluid level within range?
Does the parking brake hold the vehicle?
Is the ABS or brake warning light on?

symptoms.label: Pulls to one side when braking

questions.text: Does it shift smoothly through all gears?
Is the transmission fluid level within range?
Is there a visible fluid leak?
Is a transmission warning light on?

symptoms.label: Loses drive or will not engage a gear

questions.text: Is steering free play normal?
Does the vehicle track straight?
Is a shock absorber leaking?
Is the power steering warning light on?
Are tire pressures at the placard value?
Is tread wear even across the tire?
Are all wheel nuts present and tight?
Is a usable spare or repair kit on board?
Is the coolant level within range?
Is there a visible coolant leak?
Does the radiator fan operate?
Is the temperature warning light on?

symptoms.label: Coolant in oil, or oil in coolant

questions.text: Does the system cool the cabin?
Does the compressor engage?
Is airflow at the vents normal?
Is the cabin air filter clean?

symptoms.label: Oily refrigerant leak at lines or condenser

rules.observation: Oil pressure warning light reported on.
rules.reason: Running without oil pressure can seize the engine and cause sudden loss of drive.
rules.action: Do not run the engine. Check oil level and pressure before further use.

rules.observation: Fuel leak or strong fuel smell reported.
rules.reason: Leaking fuel is a fire risk.
rules.action: Remove the vehicle from use and repair the leak before it is driven.

rules.observation: Visible oil or fuel leak recorded.
rules.reason: A leak lowers fluid levels and can reach hot surfaces.
rules.action: Locate the source and repair the leak.

rules.observation: Engine oil level recorded outside range.
rules.reason: Incorrect oil level can damage the engine.
rules.action: Correct the oil level and check for leaks or consumption.

rules.observation: Check engine light recorded on.
rules.reason: The engine control module has stored a fault.
rules.action: Read the fault codes and record them on this assessment.

rules.observation: Knocking or rattling noise reported.
rules.reason: Internal knocking can indicate bearing or combustion damage.
rules.action: Have a mechanic diagnose the noise before extended use.

rules.observation: Misfire or rough running reported.
rules.reason: Misfires reduce power and can damage the catalytic converter.
rules.action: Read fault codes and inspect ignition and fuel delivery.

rules.observation: Loss of power reported.
rules.reason: Loss of power has several possible causes that need diagnosis.
rules.action: Read fault codes and inspect air and fuel delivery.

rules.observation: Excessive exhaust smoke reported.
rules.reason: Smoke can indicate burning oil, coolant or excess fuel.
rules.action: Have the smoke colour and cause diagnosed.

rules.observation: Hard starting reported.
rules.reason: Hard starting can come from the battery, fuel or ignition systems.
rules.action: Check battery, starter and fuel delivery.

rules.observation: Burning smell or melted wiring reported.
rules.reason: Overheated wiring is a fire risk.
rules.action: Disconnect the battery and remove the vehicle from use until the wiring is repaired.

rules.observation: Swollen or leaking battery reported.
rules.reason: A damaged battery can release acid and flammable gas.
rules.action: Replace the battery, handling it with protective equipment.

rules.observation: Battery or charging warning light recorded on.
rules.reason: The charging system may not be keeping the battery charged.
rules.action: Test the alternator and battery.

rules.observation: An exterior light is recorded as not working.
rules.reason: Failed lights reduce visibility to other road users.
rules.action: Replace the failed lamp before rental use.

rules.observation: Battery voltage with the engine off is {value} V, below 12.0 V.
rules.reason: A rested 12 V battery below 12.0 V is significantly discharged.
rules.action: Recharge and load-test the battery.

rules.observation: Charging voltage is {value} V, below 13.0 V.
rules.reason: A 12 V system normally charges above 13 V, so the alternator may be underperforming.
rules.action: Test the alternator and drive belt.

rules.observation: Charging voltage is {value} V, above 15.0 V.
rules.reason: Overcharging can damage the battery and electronics.
rules.action: Test the voltage regulator.

rules.observation: Cranking voltage is {value} V, below 9.6 V.
rules.reason: A healthy 12 V battery normally stays above about 9.6 V while cranking.
rules.action: Load-test or replace the battery.

rules.observation: Slow cranking reported.
rules.reason: Slow cranking often comes before a battery or starter failure.
rules.action: Test the battery and starter.

rules.observation: Dim or flickering lights reported.
rules.reason: Unstable voltage can indicate charging or connection faults.
rules.action: Check the alternator, ground points and connections.

rules.observation: Corroded battery terminals reported.
rules.reason: Corrosion adds resistance and can cause starting faults.
rules.action: Clean and protect the terminals.

rules.observation: Brake pedal sinks to the floor.
rules.reason: This indicates possible loss of hydraulic braking.
rules.action: Do not drive. Inspect the hydraulic system before any further use.

rules.observation: Brake fluid leak reported.
rules.reason: A leak can cause loss of braking.
rules.action: Do not drive. Repair the leak and bleed the system.

rules.observation: Metal-on-metal grinding reported.
rules.reason: Pad friction material may be gone, which greatly reduces braking.
rules.action: Remove from use. Replace pads and inspect the rotors.

rules.observation: Brake pedal recorded as not firm.
rules.reason: A soft pedal can indicate air or a leak in the hydraulic system.
rules.action: Do not drive until the hydraulic system has been inspected.

rules.observation: Front pad thickness is {value} mm, below 2.0 mm.
rules.reason: Pads near their backing plate lose braking performance.
rules.action: Remove from use and replace the front pads.

rules.observation: Rear pad or shoe thickness is {value} mm, below 2.0 mm.
rules.reason: Friction material near its limit loses braking performance.
rules.action: Remove from use and replace the rear friction material.

rules.observation: Front pad thickness is {value} mm, below 3.0 mm.
rules.reason: Pads this thin are close to their service limit.
rules.action: Schedule front pad replacement soon.

rules.observation: Rear pad or shoe thickness is {value} mm, below 3.0 mm.
rules.reason: Friction material this thin is close to its service limit.
rules.action: Schedule rear brake service soon.

rules.observation: Brake fluid level recorded outside range.
rules.reason: Low fluid can indicate a leak or worn pads.
rules.action: Inspect for leaks and pad wear, then correct the level.

rules.observation: Parking brake recorded as not holding.
rules.reason: The vehicle may roll when parked.
rules.action: Adjust or repair the parking brake before rental use.

rules.observation: ABS or brake warning light recorded on.
rules.reason: ABS or base braking may be degraded.
rules.action: Read fault codes and inspect the brake system.

rules.observation: Vehicle pulls to one side when braking.
rules.reason: Uneven braking can reduce stability during an emergency stop.
rules.action: Inspect calipers, hoses and pads on both sides.

rules.observation: Vibration when braking reported.
rules.reason: This commonly indicates rotor runout or uneven deposits.
rules.action: Measure rotor runout and thickness.

rules.observation: Squealing when braking reported.
rules.reason: Squeal can come from wear indicators or glazing.
rules.action: Measure pad thickness at the next opportunity.

rules.observation: Loses drive or will not engage a gear.
rules.reason: Sudden loss of drive can leave the vehicle stranded in traffic.
rules.action: Remove from use until the transmission has been diagnosed.

rules.observation: Visible transmission fluid leak recorded.
rules.reason: Low fluid causes rapid internal wear.
rules.action: Repair the leak and correct the fluid level.

rules.observation: Transmission fluid level recorded outside range.
rules.reason: Incorrect fluid level causes slipping and heat damage.
rules.action: Correct the level and check for leaks.

rules.observation: Transmission slipping reported.
rules.reason: Slipping indicates clutch or fluid problems and worsens with use.
rules.action: Have the transmission diagnosed.

rules.observation: Burnt transmission fluid smell reported.
rules.reason: Burnt fluid indicates overheating.
rules.action: Inspect the fluid and have the transmission diagnosed.

rules.observation: Transmission warning light recorded on.
rules.reason: The control module has detected a transmission fault.
rules.action: Read fault codes and record them on this assessment.

rules.observation: Transmission fluid temperature is {value} °C, above 120 °C.
rules.reason: Sustained high temperature degrades the fluid.
rules.action: Inspect the cooler and fluid condition.

rules.observation: Harsh or delayed shifts reported.
rules.reason: This can come from fluid condition or control faults.
rules.action: Check the fluid and read fault codes.

rules.observation: Whining or grinding transmission noise reported.
rules.reason: Noise can indicate bearing wear or low fluid.
rules.action: Check the fluid level and have the noise diagnosed.

rules.observation: Loose steering or excessive play reported.
rules.reason: Excessive play can reduce control of the vehicle.
rules.action: Do not drive until steering joints have been inspected.

rules.observation: Broken spring or mount reported.
rules.reason: A failed spring or mount can affect steering and stability.
rules.action: Remove from use and repair the suspension.

rules.observation: Steering free play recorded as abnormal.
rules.reason: Abnormal play can reduce control of the vehicle.
rules.action: Inspect tie rods and the steering rack before further use.

rules.observation: Steering wheel free play is {value} mm, above 30 mm.
rules.reason: This is above the general limit often used in inspections.
rules.action: Inspect the steering system against the manufacturer limit.

rules.observation: Vehicle recorded as not tracking straight.
rules.reason: This can indicate alignment or suspension damage.
rules.action: Check alignment and suspension components.

rules.observation: Leaking shock absorber recorded.
rules.reason: A leaking damper reduces stability and braking grip.
rules.action: Replace the shock absorber.

rules.observation: Power steering warning light recorded on.
rules.reason: Steering assist may be lost.
rules.action: Read fault codes and inspect the steering system.

rules.observation: Vehicle pulls to one side.
rules.reason: This can indicate alignment, tire or suspension faults.
rules.action: Check tires and alignment.

rules.observation: Clunking over bumps reported.
rules.reason: This commonly indicates worn bushings or links.
rules.action: Inspect bushings and links.

rules.observation: Excessive bouncing reported.
rules.reason: This commonly indicates worn dampers.
rules.action: Test the shock absorbers.

rules.observation: Uneven ride height reported.
rules.reason: This can indicate a sagging spring.
rules.action: Measure ride height and inspect the springs.

rules.observation: Tire sidewall bulge reported.
rules.reason: A bulge means internal damage, and the tire can fail suddenly.
rules.action: Do not drive. Replace the tire.

rules.observation: Exposed cords or deep cut reported.
rules.reason: Exposed cords can lead to a blowout.
rules.action: Do not drive. Replace the tire.

rules.observation: Loose or missing wheel nuts reported.
rules.reason: A wheel can detach.
rules.action: Do not drive. Fit and torque all wheel nuts.

rules.observation: Wheel nuts recorded as loose or missing.
rules.reason: A wheel can detach.
rules.action: Do not drive. Fit and torque all wheel nuts.

rules.observation: Cracked or bent rim reported.
rules.reason: A damaged rim can lose pressure or fail.
rules.action: Remove from use and replace the wheel.

rules.observation: Lowest tread depth is {value} mm, below 1.6 mm.
rules.reason: Below the 1.6 mm wear indicator, wet grip is severely reduced.
rules.action: Do not rent the vehicle. Replace the tire.

rules.observation: Lowest tread depth is {value} mm, below 3.0 mm.
rules.reason: Wet grip falls noticeably as tread approaches the 1.6 mm limit.
rules.action: Schedule tire replacement soon.

rules.observation: Lowest tire pressure is {value} psi, below 20 psi.
rules.reason: This is far below the usual car placard range, and an underinflated tire can overheat.
rules.action: Inflate to the placard value and check for a puncture.

rules.observation: Oldest tire age is {value} months, above 10 years.
rules.reason: Rubber degrades with age even when tread remains.
rules.action: Inspect closely and plan replacement.

rules.observation: Uneven tread wear reported.
rules.reason: This can indicate alignment or pressure problems.
rules.action: Check alignment and inflation.

rules.observation: Vibration at speed reported.
rules.reason: This commonly indicates wheel imbalance or tire damage.
rules.action: Balance the wheels and inspect the tires.

rules.observation: Engine overheating reported.
rules.reason: Continued running can destroy the engine and strand the vehicle.
rules.action: Stop running the engine. Let it cool, then find the cause before further use.

rules.observation: Steam from the engine bay reported.
rules.reason: Pressurized hot coolant may be escaping and can cause burns.
rules.action: Stop the engine and do not open the cap while hot. Inspect after cooling.

rules.observation: Coolant in oil, or oil in coolant, reported.
rules.reason: This can indicate a head gasket or cooler failure.
rules.action: Stop using the engine until pressure and leak tests are done.

rules.observation: Coolant temperature is {value} °C, at or above 120 °C.
rules.reason: This is well above the normal operating range of most engines.
rules.action: Stop running the engine and find the cause before further use.

rules.observation: Coolant temperature is {value} °C, at or above 110 °C.
rules.reason: This is above the usual operating range of most engines.
rules.action: Inspect the thermostat, fan and coolant level.

rules.observation: Temperature warning light recorded on.
rules.reason: The engine may be overheating.
rules.action: Stop running the engine and inspect the cooling system.

rules.observation: Coolant level recorded outside range.
rules.reason: Low coolant can cause overheating.
rules.action: Correct the level once cool, and pressure-test for leaks.

rules.observation: Visible coolant leak recorded.
rules.reason: A leak can lead to overheating.
rules.action: Repair the leak.

rules.observation: Radiator fan recorded as not operating.
rules.reason: The engine can overheat at low speed.
rules.action: Test the fan, relay and fuse.

rules.observation: Temperature gauge fluctuation reported.
rules.reason: This can indicate a thermostat fault or air in the system.
rules.action: Test the thermostat and bleed the system.

rules.observation: Sweet coolant smell reported.
rules.reason: This can indicate a small coolant leak.
rules.action: Pressure-test the cooling system.

rules.observation: Burning smell from the vents reported.
rules.reason: This can indicate an overheated blower motor or wiring.
rules.action: Switch the system off and inspect the blower motor and wiring before use.

rules.observation: Oily refrigerant leak reported.
rules.reason: A leak reduces cooling and can damage the compressor.
rules.action: Leak-test and repair using certified refrigerant equipment.

rules.observation: Compressor recorded as not engaging.
rules.reason: The system cannot cool without the compressor running.
rules.action: Check refrigerant pressure, the clutch and its fuse.

rules.observation: System recorded as not cooling the cabin.
rules.reason: Cooling has been lost, which affects rental comfort.
rules.action: Check refrigerant charge, compressor and condenser.

rules.observation: System blows warm air.
rules.reason: Cooling has been lost, which affects rental comfort.
rules.action: Check refrigerant charge, compressor and condenser.

rules.observation: Center vent temperature is {value} °C, above 18 °C.
rules.reason: A working system on maximum cooling normally delivers cooler air, depending on ambient temperature.
rules.action: Compare with ambient temperature and check refrigerant charge.

rules.observation: Water leaking into the cabin reported.
rules.reason: This commonly indicates a blocked evaporator drain.
rules.action: Clear the evaporator drain.

rules.observation: Noisy compressor reported.
rules.reason: Noise can come before compressor failure.
rules.action: Inspect the compressor and its mounting.

rules.observation: Vent airflow recorded as abnormal.
rules.reason: This commonly indicates a blocked filter or blower fault.
rules.action: Check the cabin filter and blower motor.

rules.observation: Cabin air filter recorded as dirty.
rules.reason: A dirty filter reduces airflow and air quality.
rules.action: Replace the cabin filter.

rules.observation: Musty smell reported.
rules.reason: This commonly indicates moisture or growth on the evaporator.
rules.action: Clean the evaporator and replace the cabin filter.
